newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Independent unions form new S.African federation.
newsitem.headline: Independent unions form new S.African federation.

text.p: Two independent South African labour groups said on Monday they were uniting to form new federation with over half a million members.

The new group, the Federation of Unions of South Africa (Fedusa), unites the Federation of South African Labour Unions (Fedsal) and the Federation of Organisations Representing Civil Employees, they said in a statement.
Organisers said Fedusa, which comes into being on April 1, will number over 500,000 employees from 25 workers' organisations.

It will include technicians, administrative workers, general assistants, nurses, doctors, teachers and other skilled and semi-skilled employees from the private and public sectors, the statement said.
Fedusa's founding principles include political independence, equal opportunities, professionalism, disciplined action and "support for balanced policies".

Fedusa will take the place of Fedsal in South Africa's National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac), which groups the country's other major labour federations, Cosatu and Nactu, with the government and business representatives.
